Slot width 1.0 mm nominal equals the PD2 X-value with no tolerance.

KR-PR-001 presented as a datasheet comparison ('SCWT ... from the datasheet, typically a few microseconds') although the selected C4MS025120K has no published withstand time (mosfet.json, gate_driver.json); the rule's verification method is measurement and the actual design values (0.55-1.07 us response vs <= 1.5 us requirement) are not referenced.

KR-SN-001 human-review items are surfaced (correct) but on stale parts: RECOM R12P2 / Murata MGJ2 instead of the selected UCC14141-Q1 bias module, and a generic relay instead of the selected Omron G9EA-1 DC12 whose coil-to-contact insulation is the real reinforced-barrier question.

SKILL-003 / KR-CAP-001 discharge sizing left parametric (50-200 uF) although the capacitor agent fixed 40 uF / 120 uF; the '60 s + label' recommendation was not re-evaluated at the actual ~4.5 W cost of the compliant 5 s option; the bleeder part choice (PR02) duplicates the capacitor agent's ownership (CRCW2512 chains).
Design-basis seed 'SELV control domain' changed to PELV (SGND bonded to PE) without marking it as a deviation; assumptions register A-23 reserves this as a human decision.

Correct or substantiate the '6.4 mm at 4080 V' statement (reproducible values: 3.1 mm from the impulse column, ~3.9 mm from steady-state/TOV clearance values); show the Table 9 rows used.

Section 6, candidates and open issues: replace RECOM R12P21503D / Murata MGJ2 with the selected UCC14141-Q1 (VIOWM 1500 Vrms / 2121 VDC, VIOTM 8 kVpk, > 8 mm, CTI > 600; passes 440 V DC reinforced on datasheet evidence; certificate status open; slot under body) and name the Omron G9EA-1 DC12 relay: its coil-to-contact insulation must be shown reinforced for 440 V DC (6 kV impulse basis, >= 8.8-10 mm creepage) or the coil circuit moved behind a separate reinforced barrier; verify against the fetched Omron datasheet.

summary: All fourteen stated calculations were recomputed from the given inputs and agree numerically (input currents, fuse margin, SW rms, 440 V creepage interpolation, IPC-2221B spacing, bleeder values, IPC-2221 widths, via resistance/current, Y-capacitor current, I2t, VIN-VOUT); the impulse, clearance and creepage table values match IEC 60664-1 Tables F.1/F.2/F.4 and the insulation-coordination logic (OVC II at the 600 V row -> 4 kV basic / 6 kV reinforced, reinforced creepage 2 x basic, never below clearance, strict 'other insulators' column adopted) is sound and conservative; reference-instance values were not copied and human-review rules were surfaced. Corrections are required for: (1) the slot creepage model - 'gap + 2 x thickness' is physically wrong for a through-slot and the agent's 1 mm end extension gives only 7.9-8.3 mm around the slot ends, below its own 9.0 mm rule (need >= 2.5 mm, and slot width >= 1.0 mm after tolerance); (2) the unreproducible '6.4 mm' TOV clearance figure (3.1-3.9 mm from the quoted tables; DRC values unaffected); (3) stale consistency with sibling areas - the bias module is UCC14141-Q1 (passes), the relay is the Omron G9EA-1 whose coil-contact insulation is the real reinforced-barrier question, the banks are 40 uF / 120 uF so the compliant 5 s passive discharge costs only ~4.5 W, and the power board is 2.0 mm; (4) omissions - heatsink NTC on the PE sink, TO-247 lead-to-sink clearance and pad-edge creepage (KR-TH-002), fuse ineffectiveness with a current-limited source, no published SCWT for the selected device, and the unflagged SELV -> PELV change. Standards clause texts (61800-5-1 4.3.11, 6.5.2, 4.3.3, 62477-1 numbering, touch-current limit) remain unverified in this run, as the agent itself marks.
